precepts.text: The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old; I was set up from everlasting. Wisdom and Christ are interchangeable here, because Christ is the ultimate wisdom.
precepts.point: Wisdom hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars. Seven pillars: complete wisdom.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“Wisdom hath builded her house”. Who is this wisdom? Go back a chapter, where wisdom speaks: “The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old. I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.”

This is going into Christ and wisdom, one and the same, interchangeable. Christ is the ultimate wisdom, the complete wisdom, set up from everlasting before the earth was.

That is why chapter 9 says wisdom “hath hewn out her seven pillars”. Seven represents completion, and Christ is complete wisdom. The house wisdom built stands on him, the one the Lord possessed in the beginning of his way.

precepts.text: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs. Those are the durable riches Proverbs 8 speaks of.
precepts.point: Riches and honor are with me, durable riches and righteousness. My fruit is better than gold. The riches we want are not money but the word dwelling in us richly.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Wisdom says, “Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness. My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold.” What are those riches? Colossians shows it: “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.”

The riches we are looking for are not money, though people think they are. We need the durable riches, which is wisdom: the word of Christ dwelling in us richly. And this is what we are supposed to do with it: teach and admonish one another.

God says, I am giving it to you. But you are walking in hypocrisy, distracted by covetousness, and a man’s life does not consist of the abundance of what he has. That was not their kingdom at that point, and all of this is coming to an end anyway. God has something far better than what you are looking at, and you are about to throw it away for this world.

Now you understand what the scripture is saying, so you have no excuse. Much is given, so much is required, and the one who knew will be beaten with many stripes. So I have to walk in that, stand in that space and be that, or get ready to get beat. The durable riches of Proverbs 8 are the word living in us richly, and they have to be walked in.

precepts.text: By me princes rule; I love them that love me; those that seek me early shall find me; riches and honour are with me, yea, durable riches and righteousness. If you are not seeking him, he does not love you.
precepts.point: Solomon as a youth asked for an understanding heart to judge the people, not long life, riches, or his enemies' lives, and the Lord gave him what he did not ask as well. Seek ye first the kingdom and the rest is added. Wisdom of Solomon 7:6-13: he preferred her before sceptres and thrones, loved her above health and beauty, and did not hide her riches; Sirach 4:23, hide not thy wisdom in her beauty. Our conversation should be in the scriptures.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
How do we seek wisdom? Wisdom answers in Proverbs: “By me princes rule, and nobles, even all the judges of the earth.” The Lord sets up all the kings and princes on the earth, and Christ is the wisdom of God.

“I love them that love me”: the Lord only loves those who love him. If you are not seeking him, he does not love you. “and those that seek me early shall find me.” We have a chance right now, in the midst of these wars and rumours of wars: we have to seek the Lord early, right now.

“Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness.” Riches and honour are with Christ. Durable riches are not temporal, not temporary; they last a long time, forever, eternal. “My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold; and my revenue than choice silver.”

That is how wisdom exalts her children and lays hold of them that seek her: she loves those who love her, she is found by those who seek her early, and she gives them lasting riches and righteousness.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is to hate evil: pride, arrogancy, the evil way and the froward mouth.
precepts.point: Take heed of what is around you before you fall into sin.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
“A wise man will fear in every thing, and in the day of sinning he will beware of offence.” A wise man or woman, a brother or sister who applies the commandments, fears in everything. Why does he fear? What is the fear of the Lord? “The fear of the Lord is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.”

The fear of the Lord is to despise and loathe evil and everything that comes in the package with it. Pride is evil in the eyesight of the Lord, and a lot of us have a lot of it: you can’t tell me nothing, I’m older than you. Some sisters say, I want an older sister over me, not a younger one; brothers say, I want an older brother over me. That is pride. The Lord sent these people and put them in your life. Where someone over you has no children, leadership will pair you with someone who can help guide you with yours. You can learn from a baby; every day you wake up on this planet, you learn something.

Arrogancy: many of you cannot stand it when somebody corrects you for your own benefit. You get emotional and walk out the door: I know everything, you can’t tell me nothing. Then you are saying God can’t tell you nothing. Why are you here?

The froward mouth is that disrespectful, childlike, churlish mouth. A lot of you sisters are known for it with the new sisters coming in; some brothers are nasty too. New members come through the door and don’t want to come back because you are nasty. You have to soften, remove that man spirit, have a charitable spirit, kill that old man and that old woman. Christ said whoever offends one of his little ones, better a millstone be hanged about his neck. You have a judgment coming for that.

Does the Lord like those attributes? No: “do I hate.” So do a checkup from the neck up. Write it on the mirror: I deal with pride, arrogancy, an evil eye toward my brothers and sisters. Read your four chapters a day, because you will give account for yourself alone. That is the fear the wise man has, and why in the day of sinning he beware of offence.

precepts.text: Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice is to the sons of man.
precepts.point: A sister helping to build up other sisters new in the congregation is right, and the sisters bless the nation with real talents, raising the children in the commandments, and the aged women teaching the young women. But teaching and leading the nation is not the place the Most High set for her.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

precepts.why: “Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice is to the sons of man.” Wisdom calls to men, and the leadership of the nation belongs to men; that is why Moses asked the Lord to set a man over the congregation to go out and come in before them.

precepts.text: Doth not wisdom cry and understanding put forth her voice.
precepts.point: They went throughout all the cities and taught the people, the same pattern we follow, going out into the streets to teach.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“Doth not wisdom cry? and understanding put forth her voice?”

Wisdom cries out to the people. That is what the teachers Jehoshaphat sent out did: they carried the book of the law of the Lord through all the cities of Judah “and taught the people”, putting forth the voice of understanding where the people were.

precepts.text: She standeth in the high places, at the gates, at the entry of the city.
precepts.point: They went throughout all the cities and taught the people, the same pattern we follow, going out into the streets to teach.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“She standeth in the top of high places, by the way in the places of the paths. She crieth at the gates, at the entry of the city, at the coming in at the doors.”

Wisdom does not stay hidden; she goes where the people are, to the gates and the entry of the city. So did the princes and Levites who “went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people”, and so do we, going out into the streets to teach.

precepts.text: Wisdom's call is unto men and her voice to the sons of men, a rally cry for men.
precepts.point: They went throughout all the cities and taught the people, the same pattern we follow, going out into the streets to teach.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice is to the sons of man.”

Wisdom's call is unto men, a rally cry for men. Jehoshaphat sent men, his princes, Levites and priests, to teach in the cities of Judah with the book of the law of the Lord.

precepts.text: The Lord possessed Christ in the beginning of His way, set up from everlasting, before the mountains were settled.
precepts.point: We are like grass which groweth up; in the morning it flourisheth and groweth up, in the evening it is cut down and withereth. Our youth is like a blade of grass, green and healthy, but the glory of it fades away.

note.label: Psalm 90: Teach Us to Number Our Days

precepts.why:
“Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.” Proverbs speaks of the one who was with him then: “The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old. I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was. When there were no depths, I was brought forth; when there were no fountains abounding with water. Before the mountains were settled, before the hills was I brought forth”.

The Lord possessed Christ in the beginning of his way, set up from everlasting, before the mountains were settled. The same words Moses uses of the Most High, before the mountains, from everlasting, are used of Christ being brought forth.

So the Lord who has been our dwelling place in all generations has been God from everlasting, and Christ was with him before the earth was.

precepts.text: Wisdom is plain and easily seen by those that love and seek her.
precepts.point: Like Christ saying he that has ears let him hear, everyone has ears, but only the one with understanding truly hears the wisdom coming out.

note.label: Proverbs 8: Wisdom Crieth in the Streets and Christ Set Up from Everlasting

precepts.why:
“They are all plain to him that understandeth, and right to them that find knowledge.” Wisdom's words are plain, but plain to a certain one: him that understands and them that find knowledge. Like Christ saying he that has ears let him hear, everyone has ears, but only the one with understanding truly hears the wisdom coming out.

Wisdom of Solomon says the same: “Wisdom is glorious, and never fadeth away: yea, she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her.” She is easily seen, but of them that love her; found, but of such as seek her. Wisdom is plain to those that love and seek her.

So wisdom is not hidden; the difference is in the one hearing. Her words are excellent and right, all in righteousness, and to the one who loves and seeks her they are easily seen.

precepts.text: Unto the pure all things are pure, but unto the defiled nothing is pure, even their mind and conscience being defiled.
precepts.point: Like Christ saying he that has ears let him hear, everyone has ears, but only the one with understanding truly hears the wisdom coming out.

note.label: Proverbs 8: Wisdom Crieth in the Streets and Christ Set Up from Everlasting

precepts.why:
“All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; there is nothing froward or perverse in them. They are all plain to him that understandeth, and right to them that find knowledge.” Wisdom's words have nothing froward or perverse in them, yet they are only plain and right to some.

Paul shows why: “Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled.” Unto the pure all things are pure, but unto the defiled nothing is pure, even their mind and conscience being defiled. The same right words come to two kinds of hearers, and the defiled mind cannot find them right.

Everyone has ears, but only the one with understanding truly hears the wisdom coming out. The pure understand her; the defiled and unbelieving find nothing pure even in words that are all in righteousness.

precepts.text: Lay not up treasures on earth where moth and rust corrupt, but treasures in heaven that cannot be corrupted or stolen.
precepts.point: Durable riches are not money, since lottery winners, entertainers and athletes end up broke. Durable riches are the treasures laid up in heaven, charity and helping your brother and sister in need.

note.label: Proverbs 8: Wisdom Crieth in the Streets and Christ Set Up from Everlasting

precepts.why:
“Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness. My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold; and my revenue than choice silver.” Durable riches are not money, since lottery winners, entertainers and athletes end up broke. Money is not durable.

Christ says where the durable riches are: “Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal”. Treasures on earth get corrupted and stolen; treasures in heaven cannot be.

Durable riches are the treasures laid up in heaven, charity and helping your brother and sister in need. That is the fruit of wisdom better than fine gold, and the substance she causes those that love her to inherit.

precepts.text: He that sins against the Most High wrongs his own soul, for the wages of sin is death, and they that hate Him love death.
precepts.point: They provoke Him to wrath with the works of their hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt where they had gone to dwell, cutting themselves off to become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth.

note.label: Jeremiah 44: The Judgment on the Jews Who Fled to Egypt

precepts.why:
The Lord asks the Jews in Egypt, “Wherefore commit ye this great evil against your souls”, cutting off man and woman, child and suckling out of Judah. Solomon says how sin does that: “But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul: all they that hate me love death.”

He that sins against the Most High wrongs his own soul, for the wages of sin is death. Burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt was not only provoking him to wrath with the works of their hands; it was cutting themselves off to become a curse and a reproach among all the nations. They that hate him love death, and that is the great evil they committed against their own souls.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.why: They're enemies of the gospel. They can repent, though, because they are beloved. But if they don't repent: “But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul: all they that hate me love death.” So Christ said, if you hate me, you love death. That's a cold deal right there.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why:
He is Alpha and Omega, which is Greek for the beginning and the ending. What does he mean by that? “The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.” The Lord possessed me in the beginning. “I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was. When there were no depths, I was brought forth; when there were no fountains abounding with water. Before the mountains were settled, before the hills was I brought forth: While as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the highest part of the dust of the world.”

“When he prepared the heavens, I was there:” You see that, heavens with an S? Meaning we have our first heaven here, which is the sky; the second heaven, which is space; and then the third heaven, which is where the Lord dwells. He is explaining why they call him the Alpha, the beginning: he was set up from the beginning, before everything else was created. Christ was the first of the Father's creations, the very first.

“when he set a compass upon the face of the depth: When he established the clouds above: when he strengthened the fountains of the deep: When he gave to the sea his decree, that the waters should not pass his commandment: when he appointed the foundations of the earth: Then I was by him, as one brought up with him:” That is why it says he is the only begotten Son. He was the first of the creation, then I was by him as one brought up with him, meaning the Father taught Christ everything. Before Michael was created, Christ was created; before Uriel and Gabriel and Raphael and all the rest, Christ was made before every last one of them. That is why John said about Christ, he was preferred before me.

“and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him; Rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth; and my delights were with the sons of men.” My delights were with the sons of men.

points: Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom: I am understanding; I have strength. Counsel is mine. So in counsel, when the word of God is coming out, who is ordaining the discussion being had? It is of the Lord. Counsel is of the Lord. So when an inquiry is being made, hey brother, you were seen doing this, that and the third, speak on it, the Lord is in the midst of that. But who else is right there in the midst? The Lord says all scripture is profitable for correction, instruction in righteousness, doctrine. But Satan will tell you this is not of the Lord.

And sound wisdom. Warning someone. I remember one time I warned a brother, listen brother, with the thing you battle with, this is not the right job for you to take. He took the job anyway. You should not be in this department, go into a department in the trade where you are by yourself, it is best to be by yourself, listen to class, do your job, because of what it is you deal with. And then months later: I have to quit this job. The job that I told you not to take. The job that I told you to make some kind of transition in. And then it becomes an aha moment. Because when the counsel being given to you is contrary to what you want to hear, you do not hear it. You do not listen, because it is not what you want to hear.
